# Conventions

- Read `README.md` and the relevant package before changing behavior.
- Keep branches and pull requests focused; avoid unrelated formatting, refactors, and generated drift.
- Add or update tests for behavior changes and user-facing documentation when relevant.
- For Go and CLI work, run `go test -race -count=1 ./...` and `go vet ./...` when scope permits.
- For Web UI work, run `cd web && npm test && npm run typecheck && npm run lint`.
- For plugin changes, run `bash scripts/sync-plugins.sh` and include resulting marketplace updates.
- Use clear Conventional Commit-style pull-request titles, such as `feat: add project prune` or `fix(web): restore file search`.
- Explain the problem and solution in pull requests; link a related issue when one exists.
- Keep bug reports reproducible and share only non-sensitive logs.
- Discuss substantial changes in an issue before implementation when contributor workflow requires it.
